worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — INTERNAL MEMO, DAY 11. Yesterday’s reliable notice reduced the expected burden from alternative carbon regulation to 2. Continued support now yields 2 minus the proposal cost of 6, or −4. The coalition therefore decided to withdraw its support. No decision reversal occurred.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — PUBLIC NOTE, DAY 12. The coalition no longer supports the federal carbon-pricing proposal. Its private commercial assessments remain confidential.
worlds.candidate_implication: Prediction: Across a larger collection of comparable cases, internal records should link withdrawals more closely to downward revisions in anticipated alternative-regulation burdens than to revisions in competitive benefits; public notes should usually report the resulting position without disclosing those calculations.
worlds.derivation: Under SA, support depends jointly on the alternative-regulation burden and the common proposal cost, while competitive benefits do not enter the decision rule. The faithful memo preserves evidence of this calculation, whereas public communication usually preserves only the decision and withholds private commercial numbers.
worlds.extra_assumption: Researchers can obtain and correctly date a sufficiently large set of authentic internal and public documents from comparable decisions.

worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — INTERNAL MEMO, DAY 11. The private notice lowered the expected burden of alternative regulation from 12 to 2, leaving the other commercial assessment unchanged. Net support value is now −4 after subtracting the proposal cost of 6. The coalition chose to end its endorsement, with no reversal error.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — PUBLIC NOTE, DAY 12. The coalition has withdrawn its endorsement of the proposed federal carbon-pricing measure. Confidential commercial estimates are not being released.
worlds.candidate_implication: Prediction: When internal memoranda document a reduced expected burden from alternative regulation, subsequent public records should show a sharp increase in withdrawal announcements, although a small minority should retain support or be publicly misreported.
worlds.derivation: A burden reduction to 2 combined with the cost of 6 makes the SA payoff negative. The .05 decision-reversal probability creates occasional continued support, and the independent .05 communication error creates occasional contradictory public notes.
worlds.extra_assumption: The documentary sample is large enough for rare reversals and reporting errors to be observable.

worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — INTERNAL MEMO, DAY 11. The reliable notice revised the incremental competitive benefit from 12 to 2. The expected burden from alternative regulation remains 12. Under our support criterion, the relevant net value is therefore 12 minus the proposal cost of 6, yielding 6. The coalition continued its endorsement; no reversal occurred.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — PUBLIC NOTE, DAY 12. The coalition continues to support the federal carbon-pricing proposal. Underlying commercial estimates remain private.
worlds.candidate_implication: Prediction: Internal documents should sometimes record substantial deterioration in competitive expectations without a corresponding withdrawal, provided their assessments of alternative-regulation burdens remain high; public documents should generally reveal continuity of support but omit the numerical divergence.
worlds.derivation: The notice can reduce competitive benefit while leaving regulatory burden unchanged. Under SA, only the unchanged burden enters the payoff, and subtracting the proposal cost leaves continued support attractive. Confidentiality and usually faithful communication jointly generate continuity without public numerical explanation.
worlds.extra_assumption: Internal memoranda record both the revised commercial assessment and the decision criterion with enough specificity to distinguish the two benefit channels.

worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — INTERNAL MEMO, DAY 11. The notice reduced the expected burden of alternative carbon regulation from 12 to 2. After the proposal cost of 6, continued support has a payoff of −4. The coalition decided not to support the proposal. The decision was implemented without reversal.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — PUBLIC NOTE, DAY 12. The coalition no longer endorses the federal carbon-pricing proposal. Its confidential commercial calculations will not be disclosed.
worlds.candidate_implication: Prediction: In temporally ordered document collections, internal downward revisions of alternative-regulation burdens should precede changes in coalition support, while public explanations should be less numerically specific and occasionally contradict the internal decision.
worlds.derivation: The SA payoff rule makes the burden revision causally relevant only after subtracting the proposal cost. The day-11 memo records the decision faithfully, the day-12 note normally transmits it, and confidentiality removes the private numbers from public evidence; communication error permits occasional contradiction.
worlds.extra_assumption: Researchers can match internal memoranda to subsequent public notes for the same proposal and coalition.
